issues.legal_issue: A plaint that is manifestly vexatious and meritless on a meaningful reading, and discloses no clear right to sue, is subject to rejection when a ground for rejection is met.
material_facts: An eviction order had been contested through trial, appeal, and revision and had been confirmed.
A later suit sought a declaration that the eviction order was obtained by fraud and collusion and sought to prevent its execution.
The Court found the pending suit to be a flagrant misuse of the process of receiving plaints and to have no survival value.
issues.conclusion: The trial court should reject the plaint under Order VII, rule 11 if a ground specified there is fulfilled.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court must read the plaint meaningfully rather than formally and reject it when it is manifestly vexatious and meritless, discloses no clear right to sue, and a specified ground for rejection is fulfilled. No earlier case is relied on for this principle.

rule.if: civil_suit and plaint_read_meaningfully and plaint_is_manifestly_vexatious_and_meritless and plaint_discloses_no_clear_right_to_sue and rejection_ground_is_satisfied

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.plaint_read_meaningfully: The court assesses the substance of the plaint rather than relying on its formal wording.
predicates.plaint_is_manifestly_vexatious_and_merit: The plaint's substance shows that the claim is plainly vexatious and without merit.
predicates.plaint_discloses_no_clear_right_to_sue: The plaint does not disclose a clear right to sue.
predicates.rejection_ground_is_satisfied: The facts satisfy a ground that permits rejection of the plaint.

issues.definition: When a civil plaint, read for its substance, is plainly vexatious, meritless, and discloses no clear right to sue, and a rejection ground is met, the plaint is rejected.

issues.legal_issue: When clever drafting creates only the illusion of a cause of action, the trial court should examine the party searchingly at the first hearing to expose bogus litigation.
material_facts: A second suit substantially copied the earlier suit and was used to obtain another ex parte injunction against execution of the eviction order.
The Court described the litigation as an abuse of process and urged the trial court to examine the party at the earliest stage.
issues.conclusion: The trial court should insist on examining the party searchingly under Order X at the first hearing when clever drafting creates an illusion of a cause of action.
issues.legal_principle: Order X of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for examination of parties; the Court said that this procedure should be used at the first hearing to uncover an illusory cause of action and stop bogus litigation early. No earlier case is relied on for this principle.

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.first_hearing_reached: The suit has reached its first hearing.
predicates.clever_drafting_creates_illusory_cause_o: The pleading's drafting creates the appearance of a cause of action that is not genuine.

issues.definition: At the first hearing of a civil suit, if drafting creates only an illusory cause of action, the party is examined searchingly.

issues.legal_issue: A suit found to have no survival value should be heard and disposed of promptly.
material_facts: The pending suit repeated an earlier challenge to an eviction order that had already been confirmed through successive proceedings.
The Court found the suit to be a flagrant misuse of the process of receiving plaints and to have no survival value.
issues.conclusion: The trial court should give the parties an immediate hearing and dispose of the suit forthwith.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed prompt disposal of a suit it found to have no survival value, after an immediate hearing of the parties. No provision or earlier case is cited as the basis for this direction.

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.trial_court_finds_suit_has_no_survival_v: The trial court determines that the suit has no survival value.

issues.definition: If the trial court finds that a civil suit has no survival value, it hears the parties immediately and disposes of the suit forthwith.

issues.legal_issue: Deterrent action should be taken when litigation is found to be motivated by vexation and altogether groundless.
material_facts: The Court characterized the litigation as an abuse of process and directed the trial court to consider whether it was inspired by vexatious motives and was altogether groundless.
issues.conclusion: The trial court should take deterrent action if satisfied that the litigation was inspired by vexatious motives and was altogether groundless.
issues.legal_principle: The Court directed the trial court to remind itself of section 35-A of the Code of Civil Procedure and take deterrent action on the stated findings. No earlier case is relied on for this direction.

predicates.civil_suit: The proceeding is a civil suit.
predicates.trial_court_finds_vexatious_motive: The trial court determines that the litigation was inspired by vexatious motives.
predicates.trial_court_finds_litigation_altogether_: The trial court determines that the litigation was altogether groundless.

issues.definition: If a trial court finds that a civil suit was motivated by vexation and was altogether groundless, deterrent action is taken.

issues.legal_issue: Special leave should be refused where the challenged interlocutory order arose from repeated and unrepentant abuse of court process through sham litigation.
material_facts: After an eviction order had been confirmed through trial, appeal, and revision, a suit was filed to challenge it and restrain its execution.
A substantially copied second suit obtained an ex parte injunction, which was later vacated; a further injunction was obtained in revision and then challenged before the Supreme Court.
The Court condemned the repeated proceedings as a gross abuse of process.
issues.conclusion: The special leave petition was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court dismissed the petition after finding that the proceedings were a gross and repeated abuse of process. The judgment cites no earlier case as a governing test for this disposition.

predicates.special_leave_petition: The proceeding is a petition seeking special leave to appeal.
predicates.petition_challenges_interlocutory_injunc: The petition challenges an order concerning an interlocutory injunction.
predicates.repeated_sham_litigation_abuses_court_pr: Repeated sham litigation has abused the court process.

issues.definition: A special leave petition challenging an interlocutory injunction order is denied when repeated sham litigation has abused the court process.
